**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, WARRANTY).**

What I found:
- **§ 5.1** gives a services performance standard ("reasonable care and skill... degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession") plus corporate authority and a narrow covenant to comply with "laws applicable to IBM's business." That part is broadly acceptable.
- **Missing entirely:** any warranty that Materials/deliverables conform to documentation, any no-malicious-code warranty, and any remedy. Document-wide searches for "conform", "malicious" and "remedy" returned nothing on point; §§ 11.1 and 12.2 impose Customer support duties and IBM-discretion maintenance only, so they don't supply a warranty remedy.
- **§ 5.4(c)** provides *all* Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out, and §§ 5.4(a)–(b) and 5.3(b) further disclaim error-free, capacity/performance and secure operation — so the disclaimer largely swallows the express warranty, approaching our walk-away position.

Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level): inserted a 90-day Materials/Deliverable conformance warranty and a no-malicious-code warranty into § 5.1, added an at-IBM's-option re-performance / repair-or-replacement / refund remedy, and prefaced § 5.4(c) with "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1". § 5.2 needed no change since it expressly preserves the § 5.1 warranties. Fallback signalled in the comment: a shorter conformance period if IBM pushes back.
